title: Relative colimits in a cocartesian fiber
statement: Use quasicategories, small coherent diagrams and colimiting cocones as in [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], cocartesian fibrations and degreewise fibers as in [def-coef-infinity-fibrations], and join cones and relative colimit diagrams as in [def-coef-infinity-relative-cone]. Let $p:\mathcal E\to\mathcal B$ be a cocartesian fibration of quasicategories, let $b$ be a vertex of $\mathcal B$, and let $K$ be any small simplicial set. Let $c:K^{\triangleright}\to\mathcal E_b$ be a cocone. For an edge $f:b\to b'$, write $f_!:\mathcal E_b\to\mathcal E_{b'}$ for the functor given by cocartesian transport. The composite $K^{\triangleright}\xrightarrow{c}\mathcal E_b\to\mathcal E$ is a $p$-colimit diagram if and only if $f_!c$ is a colimit diagram in $\mathcal E_{b'}$ for every edge $f:b\to b'$ of $\mathcal B$, including the identity edge. No existence of colimits other than these particular cocones and no weak contractibility of $K$ is assumed.

source.place: Proposition 4.3.1.10, printed pp. 265-266, specialized from locally cocartesian to cocartesian fibrations; the relative universality convention is the equivalent mapping-space formulation of Kerodon Proposition 7.1.6.19. Read directly in the IAS PDF; no Stacks tag states this quasicategorical result. Archival copy WANTED.

proof.text: Put $a=c|_K$, $x=c(*)$, and let $\alpha:a\to\Delta_Kx$ be the coherent cocone induced by the join cocone. The horn/mapping-space equivalence in [lem-coef-infinity-cocartesian-mapping-criterion] converts the given cocartesian fibration to the hypothesis of [lem-coef-infinity-pointwise-cocartesian-transport]. We may therefore use that node's natural homotopy-fiber formulas for objects and for $K$-diagrams. Every strict fiber is a quasicategory: a lifting problem for an inner horn in the fiber is a lifting problem for $p$ over the constant simplex at its base vertex, so its inner-fibration filler remains in that fiber. For an edge $f:b\to b'$, the transport functor $f_!$ comes with its transport homotopy $H:\mathcal E_b\times\Delta^1\to\mathcal E$ over $f$, from the inclusion to $f_!$, whose edges $H|_{\{y\}\times\Delta^1}$ are cocartesian. Put $\lambda=H\circ(c\times\mathrm{id}_{\Delta^1}):c\to c_f$ with $c_f=f_!c$; it is a coherent transformation of $K^{\triangleright}$-diagrams over the constant base transformation at $f$ whose vertex components are cocartesian. By the componentwise criterion of [lem-coef-infinity-pointwise-cocartesian-transport] (shape $K^{\triangleright}$), $\lambda$ is $p_{K^{\triangleright}}$-cocartesian, and likewise its restrictions $\lambda_a$ to $K$ and $\lambda_x$ to the apex are $p_K$- and $p$-cocartesian; so that node's fiber formulas apply to these very lifts. Write $a_f,x_f,\alpha_f$ for the boundary, apex and coherent cocone of $c_f$. This is a single compatible choice for all three pieces, and it is literally the cocone $f_!c$ of the statement, so no comparison between different transports is needed.

source.place: Proposition 4.3.1.10, transport of the entire given cocone; uses the pointwise transport theorem rather than the source slice comparison.

proof.text:
By [lem-coef-infinity-relative-cone-constant-test], $c$ is a $p$-colimit diagram if and only if, for every $z\in\mathcal E$, the apex square is a homotopy pullback. Write $s=pz$ and abbreviate its four corners by
$$U_z=\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal E}(x,z),\quad V_z=\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Fun}(K,\mathcal E)}(a,\Delta_Kz),\quad S_z=\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal B}(b,s),\quad W_z=\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Fun}(K,\mathcal B)}(\Delta_Kb,\Delta_Ks).$$
The top map sends $u$ to $\Delta_K(u)\alpha$. Since $c$ lies in a strict fiber, $p\alpha$ is the identity coherent transformation of $\Delta_Kb$, so the bottom map is exactly $\delta:S_z\to W_z$, $f\mapsto\Delta_K f$. All these are spaces and the square includes its specified coherent commutativity, as required by that node.

source.place: Proposition 4.3.1.10, reduction to outgoing-arrow tests; Kerodon 7.1.6.19 (02X1), colimit dual and apex formulation.

proof.text:
Here is the space calculation for that square. Form its path pullback $P_z=V_z\times^h_{W_z}S_z$ with projection to $S_z$, using the path model of [def-coef-infinity-relative-cone]. The square is a homotopy pullback exactly when its comparison $\Phi_z:U_z\to P_z$ is a weak equivalence. By [lem-coef-kan-pullback-path-comparison], $P_z$ is a Kan complex, and its projection to $S_z$ is a map of Kan complexes. Apply [lem-coef-spaces-homotopy-fiber-detection] to $\Phi_z$ over the identity of the Kan complex $S_z$. It is an equivalence exactly when its map on homotopy fibers is one for every vertex $f\in S_z$. The homotopy fiber of $P_z\to S_z$ over $f$ is naturally equivalent to $\operatorname{hofib}_{\Delta_K f}(V_z\to W_z)$: in path data a point is $(v,h,\gamma,\lambda)$, where $\gamma$ joins the image of $v$ to $\delta h$ and $\lambda$ joins $h$ to $f$. Compose $\gamma$ with $\delta\lambda$ to obtain the single path to $\delta f$; conversely take $h=f$ and constant $\lambda$. Allowing an intermediate endpoint and its path is the contractible path-space factor, so these maps are inverse up to the endpoint-preserving path homotopies, with all higher data. Consequently the condition is precisely that
$$\operatorname{hofib}_{f}(U_z\to S_z)\longrightarrow\operatorname{hofib}_{\Delta_K f}(V_z\to W_z)$$
is a weak equivalence for every edge $f:b\to s$. Empty $S_z$ is covered by the same fiber-detection theorem; no surjectivity or Kan-fibration assumption on either vertical map is needed.

source.place: Mapping-space reconstruction of the fiber test in the proof of Proposition 4.3.1.10.

proof.text:
Fix $z$ and $f:b\to s$, and use the transported cocone $c_f$ chosen in step 1. The object case of [lem-coef-infinity-pointwise-cocartesian-transport] identifies the source homotopy fiber in step 3 with $\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal E_s}(x_f,z)$. Its $K$-diagram case, applied to the constant base transformation $\Delta_K f$, identifies the target fiber with $\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Fun}(K,\mathcal E_s)}(a_f,\Delta_Kz)$; the strict fiber at a constant base diagram is exactly that functor category by the same node. Under these equivalences the actual fiber comparison is
$$\beta_{f,z}:\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal E_s}(x_f,z)\longrightarrow\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Fun}(K,\mathcal E_s)}(a_f,\Delta_Kz),\qquad v\longmapsto\Delta_K(v)\alpha_f.$$
To check the map, write the transport cylinder as $\lambda:c\to c_f$, with restrictions $\lambda_a$ and $\lambda_x$. Its coherent naturality square is $\alpha_f\lambda_a\simeq\Delta_K(\lambda_x)\alpha$. Precomposing $v$ with $\lambda_x$ and then with $\alpha$ therefore gives the same transformation and base path as first forming $\Delta_K(v)\alpha_f$ and then precomposing with $\lambda_a$. These are exactly the two precomposition maps in the transport fiber equivalences. The equality is coherent on all simplices because it is the naturality square of that single cylinder, not a separately chosen family of objectwise comparisons. Thus the calculation identifies the comparison map itself.

source.place: Proposition 4.3.1.10, comparison after a cocartesian transformation; naturality of the mapping-fiber equivalences.

proof.text: Assume first that every $f_!c$ is colimiting. For any $z\in\mathcal E$ and any $f:b\to pz$, apply the cocone mapping-space criterion of [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus] in the quasicategory $\mathcal E_{pz}$. It makes $\beta_{f,z}$ a weak equivalence, since $c_f$ is the specified transported colimit cocone. Steps 3-4 then make the apex square for this $z$ a homotopy pullback. This holds for all $z$, so step 2 proves that $c$ is a $p$-colimit diagram.

source.place: Proposition 4.3.1.10, implication from all transported colimits to a relative colimit.

proof.text: Conversely suppose $c$ is a $p$-colimit diagram. Steps 2-4 show that $\beta_{f,z}$ is a weak equivalence whenever $f:b\to pz$. Fix $b'$ and an edge $f:b\to b'$, and let $z$ vary over every object of $\mathcal E_{b'}$. These are exactly the maps $\beta_{f,z}$ required by the dual cocone criterion of [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus], so $c_f=f_!c$ is a colimit in that fiber. The quantifier includes the degenerate edge at $b$. For $K=\varnothing$, $\operatorname{Fun}(K,\mathcal E_s)$ is the one-point category, so the very same criterion says each $x_f$ is initial; for $K=\Delta^0$ it says the transported cocone edge is an equivalence. Neither direction has assumed any colimit besides the particular $c_f$, nor weak contractibility of $K$.

lean.statement: theorem fiber_relative_colimit_criterion {E B K : SSet.{u}} [Quasicategory E] [Quasicategory B] (p : E ⟶ B) (hp : cocartesianFibration p) (b : B _⦋0⦌) (c : rightJoinCone K ⟶ fiber p b) : IsRelativeColimitDiagram p (c ≫ pullback.snd _ _) ↔ ∀ (b' : B _⦋0⦌) (f : Δ[1] ⟶ B), stdSimplex.δ 1 ≫ f = SSet.const b → stdSimplex.δ 0 ≫ f = SSet.const b' → ∀ (T : fiber p b ⟶ fiber p b') (H : SSet.Homotopy (pullback.snd (SSet.const (X := Δ[0]) b) p) (T ≫ pullback.snd (SSet.const (X := Δ[0]) b') p)), H.h ≫ p = snd (fiber p b) Δ[1] ≫ f → (∀ y : (fiber p b) _⦋0⦌, IsCocartesianEdge p (lift (SSet.const y) (𝟙 Δ[1]) ≫ H.h)) → @IsRelativeColimitDiagram K (fiber p b') Δ[0] ((quasicategory_iff_of_isTerminal (pullback.fst (SSet.const (X := Δ[0]) b') p) stdSimplex.isTerminalObj₀).mpr ⟨innerFibrations.pullback_fst _ _ hp.1.mem⟩) ((quasicategory_iff_of_isTerminal (𝟙 Δ[0]) stdSimplex.isTerminalObj₀).mpr ⟨innerFibrations.id_mem _⟩) (stdSimplex.isTerminalObj₀.from (fiber p b')) (c ≫ T)
lean.note: Cocartesian transport is quantified through its actual fiber functor and coherent cylinder over each specified edge, with all vertex components cocartesian. The transported cone is c ≫ T. Ordinary join colimits are the terminal-base case of the existing relative predicate (HTT Example 4.3.1.3); fiber and point quasicategory structures are obtained directly from Mathlib, without added assumptions or postponed helpers.
